We walked in and were the only customers there. The two employees saw us but never spoke nor greeted us.
We proceeded to look at the dogs for our son. Our 17 year old Maltese passed recently and we were ready to open our hearts to a new family dog. Before we surprise our son, we wanted to see what dog he preferred.

I went to the front to ask the workers, who were lounging around, if we can see one of the dogs. I gave her my id, per her request, and she retrieved the puppy for us.
While I was standing she said, “We offer financing”… I didn’t ask for that nor do I need that since the dogs were pretty cheap, but after reading some of the reviews on here I see why they were.
I thought to myself that Not all black people need financing. Maybe she offers that to everyone. So, I didn’t entertain it.
Not wanting to settle on the first dog we saw, we asked to see another dog we were interested in.
The worker said there are only two of us in here, and that she can only show one dog. I looked around and there was only one other customer that walked in and they were just cruising, while the other worker was just sitting on the computer.
So, I figured she didn’t want to sell us the dogs. We proceeded to leave out, and my wife asked the other worker about seeing more than one dog. She said, “We only show the dog if you want to buy it”. I don’t usually just buy the first thing I see. We didn’t know which puppy we wanted. So, I can only assume that because of the way we LOOK, we can’t buy their cheap dogs.
Then the worker suggested that we go to a different pet store in the Woodlands if we want to look at dogs.
That was the best thing she said. My wife and I love to support small businesses, but as a business owner ourselves, we wouldn’t have workers that can’t respect customers.
I wouldn’t suggest anyone to support this store, unless the owner doesn’t know that this level of foolishness is going on.
As a matter of fact, not only do I not recommend this place, but when I do purchase our dog, I wouldn’t even recommend him or her to come here to take a poop at this location, until they clean up their act.

Besides that, the puppies were cute but half of them were fighting in their enclosures.

Steer clear from this place. My family and I walked in looking for a puppy, not really knowing what we wanted. Two people were working, one lady with a nose ring and another with black/green hair, "claiming" that she and the other lady were both mangers. Well neither "manager" greeted us when we walked through the door, so we decided to look around ourselves. We saw two prospective puppies that we might have chosen but were told that we could only see one because "most people come in knowing what they want." Then the lady with the green hair proceeded to say that we could go to another store in the woodlands if we wanted to see other dogs and hold more than one....??? Yeah, we will do just that because apparently this "small business" doesn't want our "big money." Very rude staff and I wish we wouldn't have driven out of our way to come here, to be treated like that. Look at how they reply to their negative reviews. That says a lot about who they are also.

I am deeply concerned by the reptile husbandry at this location. During my visit, I observed multiple ball pythons co-habitated in a single, completely bare enclosure with absolutely no hides or cover.
While I understand that retail stores need animals to be visible to customers, housing solitary reptiles together is highly stressful for them. When ball pythons pile on top of one another, they are not "cuddling"—they are actively competing for security and the best thermal zones. Furthermore, leaving timid, nocturnal animals completely exposed under bright store lights with nowhere to retreat causes chronic stress, which frequently leads to illness, immune suppression, and feeding strikes.
Even for a temporary retail environment, providing simple plastic hides or basic cover would give these animals a necessary sense of security without blocking them from view. I hope management will update their practices to reflect basic, humane reptile care standards.

My reply to owner:

I understand you had just got them in, however it should never be an option cohabitating ball pythons, even temporarily for a few hours, especially without hides.

While a few hours might sound brief, putting multiple ball pythons together without secure cover creates an immediate spike in acute stress and physical risk.

Maybe make sure you have the space available to quarantine new snakes individually so each one feels as secure as possible before heading to their forever home.

The girl with tattoos was very sweet and very friendly and I LOVE my new puppy. This poor rating is more so about the conditions they kept the puppy(s) in. I was not planning on adding another dog to my family, but when I saw this singular puppy inside of its glass prison all alone, I had to meet him. Instant connection, and the sweet girl told me he had been at the pet store since september. It is the end of December! I understand the store works with 3rd party breeders, but if the owners really cared about animals, how could they willingly and knowingly keep a dog in a tiny glass kennel for that long? After hearing about his entrapment, I did everything I could to convince my husband for the funds to bail the puppy out. I made offers and the 3rd parter breeder still had the audacity to rebuttal with higher than what I offered even though the dog had been at the pet store for months. The pet store should not do business with people like that. My dog is grateful to have a new life of freedom, but it just breaks my heart and makes me so angry that people will put their greed before an animal's well being. I'm assuming their high ticket prices are why the dogs sit, but to keep a dog in a tiny glass box with a hamster bottle as a water source for a medium sized dog is crazy work. His name is now Pablo, and Pablo will forever have grass to run around in and a family to love him.
